suggestions.topic: Acing the System Design Interview: Distributed Locking
suggestions.rationale: Distributed locking is a core pillar of high-level system design interviews that candidates routinely fail due to edge cases like split-brain scenarios and network partitions.
suggestions.hook_angle: If a system design interviewer asks how to prevent double-charging in a distributed queue, do you default to a basic SQL lock? Don't.

suggestions.topic: Python AsyncIO vs Threading: When to Stop Using Threads
suggestions.rationale: Developers frequently struggle with choosing between threads and asyncio for I/O bound tasks, leading to GIL bottlenecks and complex race conditions. This video breaks down the underlying concurrency models to clarify execution paths.
suggestions.hook_angle: Still using multi-threading for I/O heavy Python apps? You're walking right into the GIL trap—let's fix it.

suggestions.rationale: Cascading failures take down entire distributed architectures when downstream services fail. The circuit breaker pattern is essential knowledge for both production stability and system design interviews.
suggestions.hook_angle: One slow third-party API just took down your entire microservices architecture. Here is how a circuit breaker stops the domino effect.

suggestions.topic: Demystifying the Python AsyncIO Event Loop
suggestions.rationale: The event loop is a black box for many junior-to-mid developers transitioning to asynchronous Python. Visualizing task scheduling and cooperative multitasking drastically increases watch-time and retention.
suggestions.hook_angle: Async/await looks like magic, but under the hood, a single-threaded loop is juggling thousands of tasks without dropping a single frame.

suggestions.topic: Distributed Systems Architecture: Consistency vs Availability
suggestions.rationale: The CAP theorem dictates every distributed data store design, yet junior engineers frequently misapply consistency models in real-world system design interviews.
suggestions.hook_angle: Choosing a database purely for speed in a distributed system will destroy your data integrity. Let's break down CAP theorem trade-offs.

suggestions.topic: Python Memory Management: How Garbage Collection Works
suggestions.rationale: Memory leaks in long-running Python backend services puzzle developers who assume reference counting handles everything. Explaining generation-based garbage collection resolves production memory creep mysteries.
suggestions.search_evidence: python memory management and garbage collection
suggestions.hook_angle: Your Python app's memory usage is quietly climbing every hour. Reference counting isn't saving you—here is why.

suggestions.topic: Python AsyncIO Queues: Safe Inter-Task Communication
suggestions.rationale: Asynchronous workers often need to pass data safely without blocking the event loop. Asyncio queues solve producer-consumer concurrency issues cleanly when implemented correctly.
suggestions.hook_angle: Stop sharing raw global state across your async Python coroutines before you trigger a silent race condition.
